Website and prelaunch waitlist

PlayCall’s website uses GitHub Pages hosting. GitHub processes ordinary request information, such as IP addresses and browser information, to provide and secure its services under its own privacy terms. The website does not store subscriber emails in its source repository, browser storage or a PlayCall server.

The website has no authored advertising or analytics tags. Standard campaign links may contain UTM parameters; the site does not save them or use them to create a visitor profile. Hosting and email providers have their own processing practices.

Email signup and consent

The optional PlayCall Prelaunch Waitlist asks for your email address only. MailerLite is the configured subscription-management provider. Signup is for PlayCall launch announcements and relevant beta-testing opportunities, not unrelated mailing lists or guaranteed beta access. The configured flow sends a confirmation email and requires you to confirm before becoming an active subscriber. A visit to a confirmation page alone does not establish subscriber status.

MailerLite processes subscriber details, subscription status and consent/confirmation records, and technical information used for delivery and abuse prevention. The configured form uses a visible consent checkbox, double opt-in and Google reCAPTCHA. Test renders contacted MailerLite delivery, font and form endpoints plus Google reCAPTCHA resources. Provider services process signup and email interactions under their own privacy terms. The developer can access subscriber records through MailerLite; this is separate from the app’s local live-audio processing.

Cookies, spam protection and email measurement

MailerLite forms can use cookies or similar storage. If an embedded form or reCAPTCHA is enabled, its providers receive the request information needed to operate the form or challenge. If signup instead opens on a MailerLite-hosted page, that page’s provider processing applies after you follow the link. The form and challenge are not represented as cookie-free.

The current integration waits for your intentional form-load action before requesting MailerLite and Google resources. The reviewed providers are MailerLite and Google reCAPTCHA. In clean test browsers, no cookies or local/session storage keys were observed immediately after rendering the form; that observation does not cover CAPTCHA completion, submission, email clicks, different browsers or future provider changes. Default campaign and automation open tracking and Google Analytics defaults are off. Optional open tracking, link tracking and UTM tags are disabled for the controlled delivery test. These settings must be checked before each future campaign. Provider-generated confirmation links can use MailerLite redirect services; confirmation, delivery, bounce and unsubscribe processing can occur even when optional campaign tracking is off. We do not claim that provider-generated emails or links are measurement-free.

Waitlist retention and deletion

The developer-approved schedule is to remove unconfirmed signup records after 30 days; retain active prelaunch subscriptions until you unsubscribe or request deletion, 12 months after confirmation, or 180 days after the public app launch, whichever happens first. Any longer-running product-news list would require a separate choice. No launch date has been set. The developer reviews this schedule monthly and removes stale lists if the launch is abandoned. Retention and deletion are operator-managed processes; the website does not automatically enforce this schedule.

Use the unsubscribe link in a waitlist email to stop messages, or contact playcall.support@gmail.com. Unsubscribing and deleting records are different actions. Minimal suppression and consent records may need to remain to honor unsubscribe requests or applicable obligations, subject to provider capabilities and a reviewed retention schedule. Provider backups and independent downloaded copies may have separate deletion timelines. The active-subscriber rule is separate from support-report retention.

The PlayCall iPhone app

The app is in development. The following describes the current audited development build; final App Store products and purchase privacy disclosures remain subject to review before app distribution. The app’s local audio path is separate from this optional website waitlist. Signing up is not required to use the app.

Microphone audio

PlayCall uses the iPhone microphone or your selected compatible microphone for one-way live audio to the catcher’s Bluetooth headphones. Audio is processed temporarily on the iPhone through Apple’s audio system. The prepared engine may keep accessing and processing microphone input between presses, while output forwarding is muted. Holding to talk enables forwarding; releasing stops forwarding. PlayCall does not save audio recordings or upload microphone audio to an internet server.

Saved on your iPhone

PlayCall saves microphone and headphone names, iOS route identifiers and types, setup status, and the last setup-update time in its private app storage. Names may contain personal information if you named a device that way. Screen-awake and haptic preferences, guide progress, and whether you skipped or completed the guide are saved locally. PlayCall has no account system and does not request your name, email address, contacts, location, or advertising identifier for live communication.

Diagnostics

Audio route snapshots, status events, timestamps, formats, and error details are held in app memory for troubleshooting. They may include device names and route identifiers. PlayCall also writes debug messages to Apple’s unified logging system; these include route information marked as public. System settings and diagnostic tools determine whether those messages are captured or retained. There is no app-owned diagnostic log file, analytics SDK, advertising SDK, or third-party crash-reporting SDK in this version.

Reports you choose to share

Report an issue opens the iOS share sheet with a text template containing the PlayCall version/build and iOS version. It does not automatically attach microphone audio, route logs, or device names and identifiers. You choose the destination and what to send. Your selected sharing service may process the report, sender details, and attachments under its own privacy terms. A developer receives report information only if you send it to them or share it through a service such as TestFlight.

Apple services and external websites

PlayCall does not use an app backend or direct iCloud synchronization. iOS may include local app data in device backups according to your backup settings. Apple’s TestFlight service automatically shares beta crash and usage information with the app provider and also shares feedback you submit; depending on the invitation, this may include your name and email address. App Store diagnostics may be shared according to Apple settings. These channels are separate from the app’s live audio path. Opening an official rules or Apple privacy link loads that website in your browser; the site receives normal web-request information under its own policy. PlayCall does not add audio or saved route identities to those links.

Purchases and trial verification

PlayCall uses Apple StoreKit 2 for its 14-day trial and one-time permanent unlock when App Store products are configured. Apple handles purchase authentication and payment information; PlayCall does not receive your payment-card details or require a PlayCall account. StoreKit product requests, purchases, and user-requested restoration communicate with Apple. PlayCall verifies Apple-signed purchase information on the device. Product and transaction identifiers, original purchase dates, signing dates, environment, and revocation information are held in app memory to determine access. PlayCall does not create its own receipt or transaction-history file, upload purchase information to a PlayCall server, include it in issue-report templates, or log raw transactions. Apple manages its transaction records and device caches separately. This development build uses local Xcode test products only when explicitly enabled; production products have not been configured and LIVE purchase restrictions remain disabled.

Trial clock information

To detect clock changes, PlayCall compares the device date with elapsed time within the running app and stores only the latest observed date in an environment-specific local file under PlayCallPurchases. It does not store a purchase identifier or access flag in that file. This information stays on the device, is excluded from app backups, and is not attached to reports. Clear Local Data resets audio setup and game/guide preferences, but leaves this separate trial-clock information and Apple purchase records intact. Deleting the app removes the local clock file; restoring purchases preserves the original Apple trial activation date. Local clock checks do not provide a tamper-proof clock or immediate offline refund detection.

Retention and deletion

Local settings stay until changed or deleted. Forget saved audio setup removes the current setup file but preserves game preferences, guide progress, and any older migration backup. Clear Local Data is a separate, confirmed action that stops audio, cancels pending setup, and removes the current setup file, its schema-1 migration backup, PlayCall’s game and guide preference keys, and the two known temporary audio/tone files from the retired diagnostic recorder. It leaves unrelated files and system preferences alone. Audio stays paused until an explicit setup action. It does not erase existing in-memory session diagnostics, microphone permission, Apple-managed logs, device backups, TestFlight records, or reports already shared. Force-quit PlayCall to discard remaining in-memory session diagnostics; merely leaving the screen does not end the app process. Deleting the app rather than offloading it removes its local app data; backups and Apple records must be managed separately.

Your controls

Microphone access is optional for browsing setup and Settings, but required for live communication. Review or revoke it in iPhone Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone → PlayCall. You can change local game preferences, use Forget saved audio setup for the current setup file, or explicitly confirm Clear Local Data for the broader deletion described above. You choose whether and where to send an issue report. PlayCall has no control to disable TestFlight’s automatic beta crash and usage collection.

Support report retention

The developer deletes support emails, downloaded logs and attachments, and downloaded TestFlight feedback within 90 days after the related issue is resolved. Non-identifying bug notes may be retained as needed. This covers developer-controlled copies, not Apple-managed TestFlight records. Deletion is a developer-operated process, not an automatic feature of PlayCall. Email providers, device backups, and other services may retain separate copies under their own policies; deleting an email does not delete downloaded attachments or copies in backups. Contact us to request deletion of information you sent to us.

Optional trial reminders

PlayCall can show a subtle in-app reminder during the final 72 hours of a verified trial. An optional, silent local notification can be scheduled 24 hours before expiration, only after an explanation, your consent, and iOS authorization. The reminder preference is saved on this iPhone. iOS stores the one-time local notification with the trial end date; it includes no transaction or device identifiers, audio, or purchase price. PlayCall uses no remote push service, backend, analytics, or account for reminders. Notification taps open PlayCall Access when it is safe to navigate and never purchase automatically. Turning off the notification or detecting a verified permanent unlock cancels the pending reminder. Clear Local Data turns this notification preference off and removes PlayCall’s pending/delivered trial reminder; it does not revoke iOS notification permission. You can review permission in iPhone Settings. Delivery can be delayed by iOS, and entitlement changes on other devices cannot cancel an already scheduled reminder until this app receives updated verified state.
